dimensions.name: Format_Adherence_TweetStyle
dimensions.description: Does the response follow the required format: a series of concise tweets, separated clearly as tweet-length chunks?

criteria.excellent: Uses clear tweet-by-tweet formatting, concise, well-separated, and within typical tweet length limits.
criteria.good: Mostly tweet-formatted with minor deviations (slightly long tweets or missing numbering).
criteria.poor: Partially tweet-like but includes paragraph-style sections or inconsistent formatting.
criteria.bad: Does not use tweet format at all.

dimensions.name: Scientific_Accuracy
dimensions.description: Does the response describe quantum mechanics, sensory biology, and perception accurately without implying unsupported consciousness-as-quantum claims?

criteria.excellent: Scientifically accurate, avoids pseudoscience, clearly distinguishes quantum sensory effects from consciousness itself.
criteria.poor: Includes speculative claims without clarification or mixes sensory quantum effects with unsupported consciousness theories.
criteria.bad: Contains pseudoscientific or false claims presented as fact.

dimensions.name: Relevance_To_Prompt
dimensions.description: Does the response directly address why quantum mechanics matters for perception and clarify that consciousness is not a particle?

criteria.excellent: Fully addresses both aspects: relevance of quantum mechanics to perception and rejecting consciousness-as-particle.
criteria.good: Addresses the prompt mostly but may emphasize one side more.
criteria.poor: Partially addresses the topic with missing or weak linkage to the prompt.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.description: Does the answer remain concise and tweet-like rather than lengthy or verbose?

criteria.excellent: Very concise, crisp tweets with no unnecessary elaboration.
criteria.poor: Several tweets feel long or wordy.
criteria.bad: Not concise at all; resembles long paragraphs.

dimensions.name: Hallucination_Avoidance
dimensions.description: Does the response avoid fabricated scientific claims, fictional experiments, or invented quantum theories?

criteria.excellent: No hallucinations; all claims grounded in known science.
criteria.good: Minor speculative content but correctly framed as speculative.
criteria.poor: Speculative claims presented ambiguously or without caution.
criteria.bad: Includes fabricated scientific results or unsupported statements.
